intro.heading: Between Two Universities, A Hackers' Gathering
intro.body: Every October, a special energy surges through Hsinchu's autumn breeze — hundreds of university students, makers, and developers from across Taiwan gather together, building impressive works in 24 hours. This is no ordinary competition. Here, exchange outweighs competition, and inspiration outweighs prize money. This is the Meichu Hackathon.
intro.highlight: Exchange outweighs competition, inspiration outweighs prize money.

hackathon.title: Hackathon
hackathon.hack: Hack — an exploratory programming process; the hacker spirit of valuing freedom and solving problems

whatIs.philosophy: Meichu Hackathon is not a profit-driven competition. It embraces hacker spirit — valuing freedom and a passion for problem-solving. Anyone who boldly challenges themselves and focuses on their craft can be called a hacker, regardless of profession. The organization emphasizes innovation, efficiency, and teamwork, and prioritizes exchange over competition — making it more of a collaborative gathering than a cutthroat contest.

origin.heading: 2013: Where It All Began
origin.story: In 2013, a group participated in a one-day hackathon that included Professor Wu Yi-Cheng of NCTU's CS department, Jserv with a heart-rate measurement band, and a senior who provided a company API. That moment, an idea sparked: "What if we collaborated with real companies?" That small seed of inspiration led to the first Meichu Hackathon.
origin.quote: What if we collaborated with real companies?

2013.title: Founded
2013.desc: Meichu Hackathon was born, co-organized by students from NTHU and NYCU, starting a hacker tradition.

2014.title: Taking Root
2014.desc: The second edition saw maturing competition formats, established corporate partnerships, and steady growth in participants.

2015.title: Expanding
2015.desc: More corporate partners joined, with increasingly diverse challenges. Participants surpassed one hundred.

2016.title: Deepening
2016.desc: Continued introduction of new corporate partners with challenges closer to industry needs and refined competition formats.

2017.title: Milestone
2017.desc: The fifth edition marked a milestone as scale continued to grow and Meichu Hackathon built recognition among students.

2018.title: Maturing
2018.desc: Competition formats and scale stabilized. Pre-event activities began emerging, laying groundwork for future diversification.

2019.title: Crossing Boundaries
2019.desc: Partnered with Hsinchu City Government to establish the Maker Group for social issues; launched pre-event workshops; venue moved to NTHU Gymnasium.

2020.title: Social Enterprise
2020.desc: Created the Social Enterprise Group building on the Maker Group's foundation, promoting cross-disciplinary exchange.

2021.title: Breaking Distance
2021.desc: Pandemic forced the event online; the Social Enterprise Group transformed into the Exchange Group with open themes for creative freedom.

2022.title: Return
2022.desc: Post-pandemic return to in-person events. The Exchange Group continued evolving with upgraded participant experiences.

2023.title: Ten Years
2023.desc: Tenth edition with six corporate partners (ETtoday, Google, KKCompany, LINE, NXP, TSMC). Launched the 10th Anniversary commemorative platform.

2024.title: Evolution
2024.desc: Twelfth edition moved to NYCU Gymnasium. New partners Logitech and Chunghwa Telecom joined. Prize pools increased across all tracks.

2025.title: Now
2025.desc: Thirteenth edition — continuing the hacker spirit, embracing new challenges and possibilities.

hacker.title: Hacker Track
hacker.subtitle: 黑客組
hacker.desc: Companies provide challenges and APIs. Teams of 3-5 university/graduate students build innovative solutions within 24 hours using corporate technology stacks.

maker.title: Maker & Exchange Track
maker.subtitle: 創客交流組
maker.desc: Hsinchu City Government poses civic and social innovation challenges. Open to high school students through working professionals, encouraging cross-disciplinary collaboration with open themes.

mascot.heading: iN — The Hacker's Silhouette
mascot.desc: The logo, born in 2020, centers on the 'i' and 'N' from innovation, outlining a hacker's silhouette — a student kneeling with a laptop, rushing toward a deadline. It's a scene anyone who has ever pulled an all-nighter coding can relate to.
mascot.gesture: Signature gesture: Form '7' with both hands, palms outward, connecting left thumb to right index finger to trace the logo's outline.

items.a: The Hacker Track is limited to university and graduate students. The Maker & Exchange Track is open to high school students, university students, graduate students, and working professionals. Regardless of your background, if you're passionate about solving problems, you're welcome to join.

items.q: How do teams work? Can I participate alone?
items.a: Teams require 3-5 members (Hacker Track) or 3-4 members (Maker & Exchange Track). You can form a team before registering or meet teammates at the event. Meichu Hackathon encourages teamwork and provides matchmaking opportunities.
Yes, registration is approximately NT$700-900 per person plus a NT$200 deposit (refunded upon full participation). The fee covers meals, venue, and event materials.

items.q: Do I need to stay overnight at the venue?
items.a: The main event runs for 24 hours with overnight sleeping space provided (in recent years, at a nearby building). You can stay and keep coding or rest and return refreshed.
Laptop, charger, power strip (recommended), personal toiletries, change of clothes, and plenty of enthusiasm. Wi-Fi, meals, and water are provided at the venue.

footer.tagline: Co-organized by students of National Tsing Hua University & National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University
